# Alpha Source Pack Red-team Summary 2026-06-27

Generated from exported reviewed signals and exportable theme candidates. No raw source payloads are included.

## Reviewed Signals

- `signal-ai-memory-demand-remains-stronger-than-feared-705e583b` AI memory demand remains stronger than feared
  - Red-team objection: SEC filings support Micron fundamentals but do not prove industry-wide demand or market reaction.
  - What would falsify: demand pull-forward, customer concentration, margin erosion, or inventory rebuild.
- `signal-customer-commitments-and-ltas-may-reduce-micron-cyclicality-482ebcb6` Customer commitments and LTAs may reduce Micron cyclicality
  - Red-team objection: strategic agreements can reduce volatility for Micron without reducing cyclicality for the whole memory industry.
  - What would falsify: cancellable agreements, low-margin volume, narrow customer scope, or weak RPO conversion.
- `signal-rising-micron-capex-increases-medium-term-supply-catch-up-ri-ed4af457` Rising Micron capex increases medium-term supply catch-up risk
  - Red-team objection: elevated capex can reflect constrained high-value demand rather than impending oversupply.
  - What would falsify: capex concentrated in HBM, node migration, packaging, or demand-backed customer commitments.
- `signal-nand-and-enterprise-ssd-cycle-may-be-moving-into-acceleratio-70ffe31e` NAND and enterprise SSD cycle may be moving into acceleration
  - Red-team objection: Micron product milestones do not by themselves prove a full NAND cycle-stage upgrade.
  - What would falsify: product-specific milestones without pricing power, weak NAND margins, inventory rebuild, or peer non-confirmation.
- `signal-good-news-was-rewarded-after-micron-earnings-4f8d2b6c` Good news was rewarded after Micron earnings
  - Red-team objection: the current evidence confirms a US close-to-close reaction, but it does not prove global memory-chain confirmation or eliminate sell-the-news risk.
  - What would falsify: MU or storage peers reversing materially while QQQ remains firm, Asia memory names failing to confirm, or analyst revisions focusing on capex/supply-catch-up risk instead of earnings upside.

## Theme Candidates

- `TC-MU-AI-MEMORY-DEMAND-20260627` AI-linked memory demand remains strong, but expectation baseline still needed (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: Micron evidence alone may describe company-specific execution rather than a non-consensus memory-wide demand inflection.
  - Missing evidence: expectation baseline, peer official evidence, analyst revision evidence
- `TC-MU-CUSTOMER-COMMITMENTS-20260627` Customer commitments may improve Micron revenue durability, but industry cyclicality reduction is unproven (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: Customer commitments can improve Micron visibility without changing the memory industry's core cyclicality.
  - Missing evidence: contract duration details, peer customer commitment evidence, down-cycle behavior evidence
- `TC-MU-NAND-SSD-IMPROVING-20260627` NAND and enterprise SSD may be improving, but peer and pricing confirmation is missing (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: Micron product milestones and company commentary may not prove a broad NAND or enterprise SSD cycle acceleration.
  - Missing evidence: WDC official evidence, SNDK official evidence, NAND pricing evidence, inventory and margin evidence
- `TC-MU-CAPEX-SUPPLY-CATCHUP-20260627` Micron capex creates medium-term supply catch-up risk, but capex mix matters (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: Elevated capex can be a rational response to constrained AI demand rather than evidence of overbuild.
  - Missing evidence: capex mix details, peer capex evidence, utilization evidence, inventory trend evidence
- `TC-MU-US-MARKET-REACTION-20260627` US market rewarded Micron earnings, but Asia and analyst confirmation are missing (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: The evidence proves only a reviewed US close-to-close reaction; it does not eliminate sell-the-news risk or prove global memory-chain confirmation.
  - Missing evidence: Asia memory-chain confirmation, analyst revision evidence, 48-hour persistence or fade check
- `TC-AVGO-CUSTOM-AI-ACCELERATOR-DEMAND-20260627` Broadcom custom AI accelerator demand visibility may be improving, but conversion and concentration need review (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: The candidate may be consensus AI beta dressed as alpha unless contract durability and margin conversion are proven.

- `TC-ORCL-OCI-AI-INFRA-BOTTLENECK-20260627` Oracle OCI AI infrastructure bottleneck risk may be rising, but direct capex economics need review (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: This may be generic cloud risk-factor language rather than a differentiated alpha candidate until exact filing sections are reviewed.
  - Missing evidence: manual review of ORCL 10-K, capex return economics, power availability evidence, supplier-specific confirmation, customer demand conversion
- `TC-AI-INFRA-COMPONENT-SCARCITY-20260627` AI infrastructure component scarcity may extend beyond GPUs, but supplier confirmation is missing (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: This candidate could be too broad unless follow-up evidence isolates which component, supplier, and economic mechanism matter.

- `TC-AVGO-CUSTOM-AI-ACCELERATOR-NETWORKING-20260627` AVGO custom AI accelerator and AI networking demand visibility needs contract and margin review (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: This could still be consensus AVGO AI beta unless contract durability and margin economics are proven by reviewed source passages.

- `TC-ORCL-OCI-DATACENTER-BOTTLENECK-20260627` ORCL OCI data center power, site, and server availability bottleneck needs boilerplate review (Watch/draft)
  - Red-team objection: This has the highest boilerplate risk because much of the scarcity language may be risk-factor disclosure rather than a live bottleneck.
